reason: Real frontend/type-check defect on the core surface: the String methods' Int parameters are not type-checked, so `"abc".substring("1")` passes `kof check` and each target breaks differently (JVM `VerifyError`, Native out-of-bounds, Script `not an int`, JS silently converts — `bc`), while a user function's Int parameter correctly refuses `SEM014`. The String side is already guarded (`SEM051`); only the Int side is missing. Silent cross-target divergence / invalid bytecode = core correctness.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) defect on the core surface: the formatter's `formatDecl` has no case for `InterfaceDeclarationNode`/`ApplicationDeclarationNode`/`InfraDeclarationNode` and record members fall through to the class branch, so `kof fmt -w` writes the AST `toString` dump into the file and the CLI still reports "1 file(s) reformatted". Data loss on the core toolchain (LSP formatting uses the same `KofFormatter`), same family as #719.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) defect on the core surface: type lists are joined by `joinKw` (space-joined, meant for modifiers), so `implements A, B`, `throw A, B` and `<K, V>` lose their commas — the formatted file then fails `kof check` (`PARSE010`) or silently drops a type parameter (`SEM011`). Produces non-compiling output = core toolchain correctness.

Real compiler diagnostic defect on the core surface: `SEM093` (return with a value in a void function) is always emitted at `0:0` regardless of the return's real position, so the editor underlines the wrong line. `StatementAnalyzer` passes fixed 0/0; the neighbouring `SEM010` already uses the return's position since #502. Wrong diagnostic location is a core correctness bug.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) defect on the core surface: record headers lose their type parameters (`record Box<T>(T value)` → `record Box(T value)`, then `SEM011`) and a record with a superclass is printed as `record Nome(...) extends Base` (rejected `PARSE007`, since `record` only accepts the extends before the components). Formatter emits non-compiling output = core toolchain correctness.

Real frontend-position defect on the core surface: class/interface/record/enum/entity/constructor nodes store the token AFTER their body (the parser calls `ctx.pos()` at the end) and a field without an initializer stores the next member's position, so class errors land on the wrong line (`final abstract class Forma` reports `SEM069` on line 5) and `kof fmt` hoists every in-class comment one declaration per pass (40 repo files change on a second pass). Wrong source positions break diagnostics and the formatter alike; functions/methods already take the position before the body (bug 75 / #66).

Real compiler diagnostic defect on the core surface: an undefined declared type (`Strng`, `List<No>`, `criar(): Coisa`, `extends Animal`, `<T: Foobar>`) emits `SEM011`/`SEM085`/`SEM087` with the empty file and `0:0` — `DeclaredTypeChecker` calls `dc.error("", 0, 0, 0, …)` in every case, so a multi-file project cannot tell where the error is and the editor has nowhere to mark it. Wrong diagnostic location is a core correctness bug.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) SEMANTIC-CHANGING defect on the core surface: a typed local is always printed as `Tipo nome = valor`, so `val d: Int = 4` becomes the MUTABLE `Int d = 4` — someone who already hit `SEM037` ("cannot assign to immutable 'val' variable") compiles and runs after formatting. Also breaks function types (`var f: (Int) -> Int` → `(Int) -> Int f = …`, `PARSE041`). A formatter that changes semantics = core toolchain correctness.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) defect on the core surface: every untyped lambda parameter gains `: Object` (`(x) -> x * 10` → `(x: Object) -> x * 10`), an annotation nobody wrote, against the language's untyped-lambda idiom. Formatting must be identity-preserving on the language surface.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) defect on the core surface: calling the result of a call is printed as `adder(2).(3)` / `fs.get(0).(21)` — a dot before the empty method name — and the formatted file fails `kof check` with `PARSE039`/`PARSE041` (reproduced at the tip: a typed lambda inside the function is ALSO mangled into `return(Int b)-> a + b`). Formatter emits non-compiling output = core toolchain correctness.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) defect on the core surface: a generic function with a generic return is printed in the type-before-name form (`wrap<X>(X x): List<X>` → `List<X> wrap<X>(x: X)`), which does not parse (`PARSE011`/`PARSE023` — reproduced at the tip); function-type expression bodies break the same way. Formatter emits non-compiling output = core toolchain correctness.

Real CLI (`kof fmt`) SEMANTIC-CHANGING defect on the core surface: the pattern guard is printed away — `case String t if t.isEmpty(): return "vazia"` becomes `case String t:` — so after formatting `describe("oi")` prints `vazia` instead of `texto oi` (reproduced at the tip, before/after). An empty `default:` disappears from a switch statement too. A formatter that silently changes program behaviour = core toolchain correctness.

Real compiler/lowering defect on the core surface: a case guard on a switch STATEMENT (the expression form works) runs BEFORE the type test, so a value of another type hits the cast and dies (`ClassCastException` on JVM, "type cast failed" on native/Script); and `case Point(x, y) if x > 0` cannot see the destructured fields (`SEM011` on `x` — reproduced at the tip). Core parity/correctness on supported targets.
